complete_compiler_story.summary: OpenAI profiles four Australian universities redesigning learning and assessment around AI. A commissioned survey of 1,018 students found 81% use AI weekly, 28% have built an agent and 79% want more real-world practice. Examples include simulations, staged tool access and UNSW’s Can, Can’t, Must assessment framework.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Educators can classify one assignment by permitted, prohibited and required AI use, then add a simulation or reflection that reveals student reasoning. Keep the vendor-commissioned survey separate from independently measured learning outcomes.

source.title: Q3 2026 financial results
source.scope: Complete original source, evidence, controls, availability and limitations.
source.freshness_reason: Original publisher supplies a calendar date. The article is considered under the normal 72-hour fallback because the exact original publication time was unavailable.

complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Frames hosted agents as intermediaries and separates user intent from agent identity, disclosure, reputation and site policy.
complete_compiler_story.summary: Airbnb says it plans a first-half 2027 guest rollout for a visual travel agent that combines maps, photos, comparisons, calendars and itineraries instead of relying only on chat. The company expects reservation context to support after-booking help, but the interface is not yet available and the timetable remains a company target.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Travel and service teams can examine how visual options support shared decisions without treating a roadmap as a released product. Test map, photo and itinerary choices with explicit human confirmation, provenance and fallback paths.

audience_fit.review_action: Compare the two locations, fees and cancellation terms against the original listing before making a choice.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A shared shortlist with specific tradeoffs and a recorded confirmation step before booking.

complete_compiler_story.headline: Claude’s finance beta supports a read-only verification Skill

source.title: Introducing Personal Finance in Claude
source.scope: Complete original source, evidence, controls, availability and limitations.
source.freshness_reason: Original publisher supplies a calendar date. The article is considered under the normal 72-hour fallback because the exact original publication time was unavailable.

read_evidence.scope: Read the original release, eligibility, supported account data, read-only access, source verification suggestions and disconnection steps.

complete_compiler_story.related_coverage: Packages a bounded question, generated analysis, evidence check and accountable action into one reusable noncoding Skill.
complete_compiler_story.summary: Anthropic opened a U.S. beta that gives eligible Claude Pro, Max and Ultra users read-only Plaid access to selected financial accounts, including balances, limits and up to two years of transactions. This Skill defines one bounded question, transaction-level evidence, bank-statement cross-checking and unlinking when the review ends; it never permits money movement.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: Use the Skill with one account, question and date range; require a categorized answer plus cited transactions, compare totals against the bank statement, reject mismatches and disconnect the account securely when finished.
complete_compiler_story.image_alt_intent: Distinct editorial illustration for claude’s finance beta supports a read-only verification skill showing evidence, verification and human review.

audience_fit.intended_user: A person reviewing their own transactions with a bank statement or spreadsheet.
audience_fit.practical_action: Ask one bounded question about an eligible connected account and request the transaction evidence for each total.
audience_fit.review_action: Compare the returned transactions with the bank statement, flag differences and disconnect the account when finished.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reconciled summary for one account and date range, with unmatched or miscategorized items explicitly flagged.

complete_compiler_story.agent_skills_evidence: This reusable read-only Skill takes one eligible connected account, a date range and a specific question. Ask for a categorized result with its underlying transactions, compare those amounts and totals against the bank statement, flag any discrepancies before relying on the result, and disconnect after review.
